name: TDK-mlf
title: MLF2012 multilayer ferrite chip inductors, 2.0 × 1.25 mm, 0.047 µH to 100 µH
summary: MLF2012 is TDK's family of two-terminal chip inductors with a monolithic multilayer ferrite structure. The body is 2.0 × 1.25 mm and either 0.85 mm or 1.25 mm thick. Forty values run from 0.047 µH to 100 µH in ±5 %, ±10 % or ±20 % tolerance; rated current falls from 300 mA on the smallest values to 2 mA on the largest. Applications named for it include smartphones, tablets, tuners, LCD and PDP televisions, audio equipment, computers and signal processing in modules.

operation.text: Each chip is a monolithic multilayer ferrite part with a terminal electrode at either end. The series operating range is -55 °C to +125 °C.

The letter after 2012 follows the value: D for 0.047 µH to 0.82 µH, A for 1.0 µH to 4.7 µH, E for 5.6 µH to 12 µH, K for 39 µH to 56 µH and C for 15 µH to 33 µH and 68 µH to 100 µH. Q and L are measured at a frequency that falls with value: 50 MHz up to 0.082 µH, 25 MHz to 0.82 µH, 10 MHz to 4.7 µH, 4 MHz for 5.6 µH to 8.2 µH, 2 MHz for 10 µH and 12 µH and for the K grade, 1 MHz for most C values and 0.4 MHz for 33 µH. The test current is 1.0 mA up to 4.7 µH and 0.1 mA above.
0.047 µH, 0.068 µH and 0.082 µH come in ±20 % only. 0.10 µH to 12 µH come in ±5 %, ±10 % and ±20 %. 15 µH to 100 µH come in ±10 % and ±20 %.
The 0.85 mm body carries 0.047 µH to 0.39 µH and 1.0 µH to 2.2 µH; every other value uses the 1.25 mm body. Reel quantity and tape cavity depth follow the thickness.
Values of 15 µH and above are limited to -40 °C to +85 °C for both operation and storage; smaller values keep -55 °C to +125 °C.

Reflow follows the profile: 150 °C to 180 °C for 60 s to 120 s, then above 230 °C for 30 s to 60 s with a 250 °C to 260 °C peak held 10 s at most. The chip is preheated so that it is never more than 150 °C cooler than the solder it meets. Rework after mounting stays within the conditions of the delivery specification; overheating can short the part, shift its characteristics or shorten its life.
Current through the part warms it once power is on, and the set's thermal design needs margin for that rise.

Without a magnetic shield, a coil placed carelessly on the board can couple into nearby circuits and cause faults. Keep the parts away from magnets and magnetic fields, ground the person handling them through a wrist strap, avoid board flex and screw-point stress on a mounted chip, and keep them out of corrosive atmospheres such as salt, acid or alkali gases.
Unmounted parts keep for under 12 months at 5 °C to 40 °C and 10 % to 75 % RH; kept longer, the terminations may solder poorly.
